summary: Iteration 10 verified. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_iter10_payments.py (11 tests). Standalone iter10 run = 11/11 PASS. Verified POST /api/payments/checkout for medio/platino returns real cs_test_ Stripe sessions with checkout.stripe.com URLs; basico + unknown plans -> 400; unauthenticated call -> 401; GET /api/payments/status/{sid} returns {session_id, status, payment_status='pending' initially, plan} without auth; unknown session -> 404. 80% warning: fresh basico user hit 8/10 invoices (via API), /api/plan returns usage.invoices_month=8, max=10 (80%); filled to 10/10; 11th POST /api/invoices -> 403 with detail mentioning 'límite'. Regression: PUT /api/admin/plans still succeeds, propagates to GET /api/plans, and defaults (medio 9.99 / platino 24.99) restored. Frontend: /precios for a basico user shows pricing-card-basico/medio/platino, current-badge-basico, usage-panel, upgrade-medio and upgrade-platino. Clicking upgrade-medio redirects to https://checkout.stripe.com/... (verified navigation commit). /payment/cancel renders payment-cancel-page and its 'Volver a Planes' button (cancel-go-pricing) navigates back to /precios. At 8/10 invoices, /precios shows amber limit-warning + global usage-warning-banner ('Estás al 80% del límite de tu plan Básico.') with 'Ver planes' link (usage-warning-upgrade). At 10/10, both banner and warning switch to red/critical wording ('Has alcanzado el límite de tu plan Básico.'). No console errors. Full-parallel regression across iter8/9/10 (41 tests) shows 2 transient failures due to concurrent PUT /api/admin/plans between iter9 gating fixture and iter10 regression editing medio price — these are TEST parallelisation races (iter9 restores defaults while iter10 asserts its edit); not product bugs. Both files pass 100% when run individually.
critical_code_review_comments: payments_routes._upgrade_user swallows exceptions with only a log — silent failure to persist plan upgrade after successful Stripe payment would only be visible in logs. Consider surfacing metric/alert or at least marking payment_transactions row with an 'upgrade_error' field so support can reconcile.

stripe_service.create_subscription_session catches broad InvalidRequestError three levels deep — if all three attempts fail the raw StripeError bubbles as 500. Consider explicit HTTPException 502 with a user-friendly message ('No pudimos iniciar el pago, inténtalo en unos minutos').

PaymentSuccess.js polls up to 8 * 2s = 16s. For subscription mode with automatic_tax the async settlement can be longer; consider increasing MAX_POLLS or falling back to a webhook-only path with a 'ya se activará en unos minutos' message (already partially done in the timeout branch).

GET /api/payments/status/{session_id} is intentionally unauthenticated (fine because session_id is unguessable), but it does upgrade the user's plan when Stripe reports 'paid'. If session_id ever leaked in logs/referrer headers, an attacker could not upgrade another account (metadata carries user_id), but consider rate-limiting the endpoint to prevent Stripe API abuse.

Pricing.js recomputes limits directly against current (plan) fields — for admin users current.id === 'admin' but the API's /plan returns the ADMIN_PLAN with usage; isAdmin gates usage-panel but limit-warning also depends on invLimit != null which is null for admin so shows nothing. That's fine, just noting the interaction.

success_rate.backend: 100% (11/11 iter10 standalone; 39/41 in full parallel run due to test-parallel race, not a product bug)

test_credentials: admin@fiscalhub.es / admin123. Fresh basico users self-registered as iter10_*@example.com / test1234.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral basico users iter10_*, iter10ui_*, iter10warn_* registered via /api/auth/register (test data prefix). One user was pushed to 11 invoices to trigger 403 path. Admin plans were mutated during regression test then restored to defaults (medio 9.99, platino 24.99). Final GET /api/plans confirmed defaults intact.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter10 testids all validated: nav-pricing, pricing-card-{basico|medio|platino}, current-badge-basico, usage-panel, upgrade-medio, upgrade-platino, limit-warning (amber<10, red>=10), usage-warning-banner + usage-warning-upgrade (in Layout), payment-cancel-page + cancel-go-pricing, payment-success-page + success-go-dashboard/success-go-pricing. Stripe checkout endpoint really hits Stripe (~1-2s per call to sync catalog + create session). If running iter9+iter10 together, don't run them in parallel workers — iter9's admin_client teardown restores default plan prices which races with iter10's regression edit; add pytest-xdist --dist=loadfile or a lock, or run sequentially. Real Stripe hosted-page automation (test card 4242...) was NOT executed — best-effort only per the request. Payment success path is exercised through unit test on /api/payments/status returning payment_status='pending'.
rca of the issue: N/A — no product bugs. The 2 flaky regression failures in a fully parallel iter8+9+10 run are due to two test files (iter9 gating + iter10 regression) both mutating global admin plan overrides through /api/admin/plans; fixture teardown from iter9 races with iter10's assertion between its PUT and GET. Fix: run test files sequentially (pytest -p no:xdist) or use --dist=loadfile.
